answer.answer: Scrapy defaults TWISTED_REACTOR to 'twisted.internet.asyncioreactor.AsyncioSelectorReactor' so that asyncio support is enabled out of the box: asyncio and asyncio-powered libraries can be used in any coroutine, and new projects (e.g. created with startproject) need no additional setup (decision:asyncio-reactor-default, documented in docs/topics/asyncio.rst). The default is set in scrapy/settings/default_settings.py (module scrapy.settings.default_settings), line 609: TWISTED_REACTOR = "twisted.internet.asyncioreactor.AsyncioSelectorReactor". When using CrawlerRunner/AsyncCrawlerRunner the reactor must still be installed manually via scrapy.utils.reactor.install_reactor.

The default is set in scrapy/settings/default_settings.py (line 609: TWISTED_REACTOR = "twisted.internet.asyncioreactor.AsyncioSelectorReactor", next to TWISTED_REACTOR_ENABLED = True). The docs say the reason is asyncio support: this reactor lets you use asyncio and asyncio-powered libraries in coroutines, and Scrapy supports asyncio natively. The default changed from None to the asyncio reactor in Scrapy 2.13.0, where it is listed as a highlight ('The asyncio reactor is now enabled by default'). The 2.13.0 notes also say newly generated projects had used this value since Scrapy 2.7.0. With the new default, existing projects that don't set TWISTED_REACTOR also get the asyncio reactor, and they can still set the setting to choose a different reactor (gh 6659, 6713). Setting it to None makes Scrapy use any reactor that is already installed, or else Twisted's platform default.
